title: Heavily Sr-Doped La$_{2}$SrNi$_{2}$O$_{7-δ}$ as a Tetragonal Ruddlesden-Popper Phase at Ambient Pressure
authors: Yuhang Zhang, Xue Ming, Cui-Qun Chen, Wei Chen, Tian-Yi Li, Zhe-Ning Xiang, Qing Li, Bing-hui Ge, Dao-Xin Yao, Xiyu Zhu, Hai-Hu Wen
abstract: High-temperature superconductivity has been found in bilayer Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) nickelates in bulk samples under high pressure, or in thin films via compressive strain. In the superconducting state, a tetragonal structure with a straight Ni-O-Ni bond along c-axis has been commonly observed, together with the suppression or diminishing of the density-wave orders. Therefore, it remains an open question whether these factors are sufficient for achieving superconductivity at ambient pressure. Here we report the first successful synthesis of heavily Sr-doped La$_{2}$SrNi$_{2}$O$_{7-δ}$ under high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) conditions with a flux method. X-ray diffraction and scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) confirm that the material adopts a tetragonal (I4/mmm) structure with an 180$^{\circ}$ Ni-O-Ni bond angle along c-axis. Resistance measurements reveal metallic behavior with a low-temperature upturn and no density-wave features are observed. However, neither pressure nor oxygen variation induces superconductivity. Density functional theory calculations indicate that the holes introduced by Sr doping are predominantly doped into the Ni-3d$_{z^2}$ orbital, leading to the appearance of a very large $γ$ pocket on the Fermi surface at ambient pressure and significantly reducing the occupation of the Ni-3d$_{z^2 }$ orbital. Combining the experimental observations with theoretical calculations, we attribute the absence of superconductivity to the serious deviation from the half-filling state of the Ni-3d$_{z^2 }$ band, which is crucial for the interlayer antiferromagnetic interaction and thus for pairing. Our work unravels important issues for achieving superconductivity in bilayer nickelate system.
summary: This research successfully synthesizes a highly symmetric, tetragonal nickelate phase ($	ext{La}_2	ext{SrNi}_2	ext{O}_{7-\delta}$) at ambient pressure. While the material is metallic, the authors argue that the excess hole doping shifts the electronic structure away from the optimal half-filled state, thereby suppressing the interlayer magnetic coupling required for superconductivity.
main_problem: The central question is determining the necessary conditions—structural, electronic, or chemical—to achieve high-temperature superconductivity in bulk Ruddlesden-Popper nickelates at ambient pressure.
main_result: The authors report synthesizing a tetragonal $	ext{La}_2	ext{SrNi}_2	ext{O}_{7-\delta}$ phase, but attribute the absence of superconductivity to a significant deviation from the half-filling state of the $	ext{Ni}-3d_{z^2}$ band, which weakens the necessary interlayer antiferromagnetic coupling.
method: The study combines high-pressure/high-temperature synthesis, structural characterization (XRD, STEM), transport measurements, and theoretical calculations (DFT) to map the phase diagram and electronic structure.
model_or_system: The physical system is the heavily Sr-doped $	ext{La}_2	ext{SrNi}_2	ext{O}_{7-\delta}$ Ruddlesden-Popper nickelate, which is studied across varying oxygen content, pressure, and doping levels.
key_observables: Tetragonal crystal structure ($	ext{I}4/	ext{mmm}$), metallic resistance behavior, large $\gamma$ pocket on the Fermi surface, and the suppression of density-wave features.
important_parameters: Ambient pressure vs. high pressure (up to 51.9 GPa); Sr doping level; $	ext{Ni}-	ext{O}-	ext{Ni}$ bond angle ($180^\circ$ ideal); filling of the $	ext{Ni}-3d_{z^2}$ orbital.
main_assumptions: The superconducting pairing mechanism is critically dependent on maintaining the half-filling state of the $	ext{Ni}-3d_{z^2}$ orbital, which mediates interlayer antiferromagnetic interaction.
figures_summary: Figures detail the crystal structure and lattice parameters (XRD/STEM), show the temperature and pressure dependence of resistance and magnetization, and present DFT calculations illustrating the band structure and Fermi surface evolution under pressure.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the structural synthesis of the tetragonal phase, then characterizes its electronic and transport properties, and finally uses DFT calculations to explain the failure to achieve superconductivity by analyzing the orbital filling relative to the half-filled state.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the fundamental mechanism of high-Tc superconductivity in nickelates, which is a canonical problem in strongly correlated electron physics, providing crucial insights into orbital physics and doping effects.
